skos:definition: Dimensionless ratio used for stencil release in solder paste printing, defined as aperture open area divided by aperture wall area: AAR = (L×W) / (2×(L+W)×T), where L and W are aperture length and width, and T is stencil thickness.
skos:example: For a 0.30 mm × 0.15 mm aperture in a 0.075 mm stencil: AAR = (0.30×0.15)/(2×(0.30+0.15)×0.075) = 0.67, which meets the typical ≥0.66 guideline.

skos:definition: A recorded calculation of the aperture area ratio for a specific stencil aperture, based on measured or design L, W, and T values.
skos:example: Job ABC: L=0.30 mm, W=0.15 mm, T=0.075 mm → AAR=0.67 (accepted).

skos:definition: A requirement specifying the acceptable minimum aperture area ratio for a given design and stencil technology.
skos:example: Spec: AAR ≥ 0.66 for laser-cut, electropolished stainless steel stencils.

skos:definition: Diameter of a circular stencil aperture used to deposit solder paste onto a circular pad (e.g., BGA land).
skos:example: A 0.23 mm diameter circular aperture is used for a 0.40 mm pitch BGA land.

skos:definition: A measured value of a specific circular stencil aperture diameter.
skos:example: Measured with optical microscope: aperture diameter = 0.228 mm.

skos:definition: The required nominal diameter and tolerance for a circular stencil aperture.
skos:example: Spec: 0.23 ± 0.02 mm for BGA paste apertures.

skos:definition: Paste over-deposit caused by an aperture that effectively prints beyond the intended pad area—due to oversize aperture/overprint, stencil misalignment, or excessive under-stencil paste—increasing risk of bridging or solder beads.
skos:example: 0201 capacitor pads printed with a +10% overprint produce paste spreading into the mask dam and intermittent bridges.

skos:definition: Nominal diameter of a solder ball on a BGA package prior to reflow.
skos:example: Package uses 0.30 mm balls on a 0.50 mm pitch BGA.

skos:definition: A measured diameter of solder balls on a specific BGA component.
skos:example: X-ray/optical measurement: ball diameter = 0.296–0.302 mm.

skos:definition: The required nominal diameter and tolerance for BGA solder balls.
skos:example: Spec: 0.30 ± 0.02 mm diameter per component datasheet.

skos:definition: Out-of-plane deformation (bow and/or twist) of a bare or assembled PCB, usually expressed as a percentage of the board length/diagonal.
skos:example: A 200 mm PCB with 0.8 mm maximum bow has 0.4% warpage.
normative_reference: IPC-TM-650 2.4.22 (Bow and Twist); IPC-6012 (Qualification and Performance)

skos:definition: A recorded measurement of PCB bow/twist for a specific board at a stated temperature/fixturing.
skos:example: Room temperature, supported at corners: warpage = 0.38%.
test_method: Measure per IPC-TM-650 2.4.22 at stated temp
normative_reference: IPC-TM-650 2.4.22 (Bow and Twist); IPC-6012 (Qualification and Performance)

skos:definition: The allowable PCB warpage under defined conditions (e.g., room temperature and at reflow temperature).
skos:example: Spec: ≤0.75% bare board at 23 °C; ≤0.50% at reflow temperature.
normative_reference: IPC-TM-650 2.4.22 (Bow and Twist); IPC-6012 (Qualification and Performance)
normative_notes: Typical ≤0.75% RT; tighter at reflow e.g., ≤0.50%

skos:definition: Automated or manual operation that picks packaged components and places them onto printed solder paste or adhesive at specified positions and orientations.
skos:example: High-speed mounter places 0402 passives and a fine-pitch QFP within ±50 µm accuracy.

skos:definition: Planned evaluation to determine whether a product or process meets stated requirements or standards.
skos:example: First-article inspection comparing solder paste SPI data and placement Cpk to the build spec.

skos:definition: An authorized, documented action plan intended to eliminate the root cause of a detected nonconformity and prevent recurrence.
skos:example: Reduce stencil thickness from 120 µm to 100 µm and update print parameters to eliminate bridging on 0.4 mm pitch BGA.

skos:definition: A nonconforming material or process state that degrades functionality, reliability, or compliance (e.g., opens, shorts, voids).
skos:example: Solder bridge shorting pins 17–18 of a QFP device.

skos:definition: An observable outcome or state resulting from a cause or set of causes in manufacturing or use.
skos:example: Head-in-pillow (effect) resulting from warpage mismatch and insufficient time above liquidus.

skos:definition: Condition where a single stencil aperture deposits more paste than intended due to oversize aperture, double-printing, or paste scooping.
skos:example: A misprogrammed double print increases deposit volume by ~60% on 0.5 mm pitch pads, leading to bridges.

skos:definition: Solder wetting and flow beyond pad boundaries during reflow, often driven by high peak temperature, overly active flux, or low mask dam.
skos:example: On a QFN, solder spreads 150 µm into the solder mask channel and creates a short to the adjacent pad.

skos:definition: A factor, parameter excursion, or condition that can produce a defect or undesired effect when realized in a process.
skos:example: Low area ratio in stencil apertures causing insufficient paste release and opens.

skos:definition: Ambient relative humidity above the allowed range for solder paste handling or storage, promoting slump, oxidation, and inconsistent printing.
skos:example: Printing at 70% RH causes paste to slump between 0.4 mm pitch pads, increasing bridging defects.
normative_reference: Manufacturer datasheet; internal process spec (environmental controls)

skos:definition: Amount of ionizable residues on a PCB assembly, typically expressed as µg NaCl equivalent per unit area and measured by ROSE or ion chromatography.
skos:example: ROSE test result: 0.80 µg NaCl eq/in² after reflow.

skos:definition: A measured ionic contamination value for a specific unit, lot, or panel.
skos:example: Panel 12C: 0.62 µg NaCl eq/in² (pass).

skos:definition: The maximum allowable ionic contamination for a product under specified test conditions.
skos:example: Spec: ≤1.00 µg NaCl eq/in² per internal cleanliness requirement.

skos:definition: Formation of large solder beads adjacent to chip components after reflow, typically due to excess paste volume, low paste viscosity, or inadequate aperture design.
skos:example: 0402 resistors exhibit beads >0.3 mm on the component side after reflow.
normative_notes: Minimize visible solder balls/beads per A-610 guidance

skos:definition: Aperture area ratio below recommended threshold, causing poor paste release and under-deposits or clogged apertures.
skos:example: AAR=0.55 on 0.30×0.15 mm apertures in a 0.10 mm stencil results in insufficient solder and opens.

skos:definition: Solder paste metal load below specification, increasing slump and solder balling while reducing final joint volume.
skos:example: Paste measured at 86 wt% metal vs. spec 88–90 wt% leads to solder beading on 0603s.
test_method: Per J-STD-005 metal content test; gravimetric
normative_notes: Below 88 wt% considered low for stencil printing

skos:definition: Paste viscosity below the required range, often causing excessive post-print spread, bridging, or poor aperture filling.
skos:example: Viscosity 120 Pa·s (Malcom, 25 °C, 10 rpm) vs. spec 160–220 Pa·s; bridges observed on 0.5 mm pitch.
normative_notes: Below typical lower bound causes spread

skos:definition: Width of solder mask web between adjacent exposed copper pads, controlling solder spread and electrical clearance.
skos:example: Between two 0.5 mm pitch QFP pads, the mask dam width is 75 µm.
normative_reference: IPC-7351 (SM Design and Land Pattern); IPC-2221

skos:definition: A measured mask web width between specific pads on a PCB.
skos:example: Measured under microscope: mask dam = 80 µm (meets ≥75 µm requirement).
normative_reference: IPC-7351 (SM Design and Land Pattern); IPC-2221

skos:definition: The minimum allowable solder mask dam width for a design feature.
skos:example: Spec: mask dam width ≥75 µm for 0.5 mm pitch devices.
normative_reference: IPC-7351 (SM Design and Land Pattern); IPC-2221

skos:definition: Count of solder balls on a BGA or WLCSP package.
skos:example: Package has 256 balls arranged in a 16×16 array with corner balls depopulated.

skos:definition: An observed count of balls present on a specific device or lot.
skos:example: X-ray inspection confirms 256 balls; no missing balls detected.

skos:definition: The required ball count per package type and pinout.
skos:example: Spec: 256 balls; any deviation is not acceptable.

skos:definition: Printed Circuit Board substrate and interconnect structure onto which components are assembled.
skos:example: Four-layer FR-4 PCB, 1.6 mm thick, ENIG finish, green solder mask.

skos:definition: Diameter of a circular BGA land on the PCB.
skos:example: For 0.40 mm pitch BGA, pad diameter = 0.22 mm (NSMD).

skos:definition: A measured diameter of a specific BGA land on the PCB.
skos:example: Optical measurement: pad diameter = 0.218 mm.

skos:definition: The required diameter and tolerance for BGA lands on the PCB.
skos:example: Spec: 0.20–0.23 mm for 0.40 mm pitch NSMD pads.

skos:definition: A named attribute of a process parameter that can be specified, controlled, and measured (e.g., speed, pressure, temperature).
skos:example: In stencil printing, squeegee speed and pressure are controlled ParameterCharacteristics.

skos:definition: An information record capturing the measured value(s), method, unit, and context for a specific parameter.
skos:example: SPI report entry: paste volume = 350 nL, threshold = ±15%, board SN 12345.

skos:definition: A measurable attribute that inheres in a material, component, or process (e.g., thickness, viscosity, diameter).
skos:example: Stencil thickness and paste viscosity are ParameterQualities.

skos:definition: A requirement that constrains an attribute or parameter by target, tolerance, range, unit, and test method.
skos:example: Spec: stencil thickness 100 µm ±5 µm, measured per optical micrometer method.

skos:definition: Distribution of solder powder particle sizes in a paste, often summarized by D10/D50/D90 and classified by IPC types (e.g., Type 4).
skos:example: Type 4 powder: ~20–38 µm with D50 ≈ 28 µm, verified by laser diffraction.

skos:definition: A measured particle size distribution for a specific solder paste lot.
skos:example: Lot SP-22: D10=20 µm, D50=28 µm, D90=37 µm (Type 4).

skos:definition: The required particle size distribution/classification for solder paste.
skos:example: Spec: Type 4 per J-STD-005—90% between 20–38 µm.

skos:definition: Mass fraction of metal in a solder paste (wt%), affecting deposit volume, slump, and reflow behavior.
skos:example: A no-clean SAC305 paste with 88.5 wt% metal load.

skos:definition: A measured metal content for a specific solder paste lot.
skos:example: Lot SP-22 measured at 88.3 wt% metal.

skos:definition: The required metal content for a solder paste formulation.
skos:example: Spec: 88–90 wt% metal for stencil printing process window.

skos:definition: Ambient temperature range within which an opened solder paste can remain in use on the printer without degradation.
skos:example: Recommended open-life temperature: 20–25 °C on the print floor.
normative_reference: Manufacturer datasheet; internal process spec (environmental controls)

skos:definition: Recorded ambient temperature during a paste open-life interval.
skos:example: Run logged at 23 °C ±1 °C during an 8-hour open-life window.
normative_reference: Manufacturer datasheet; internal process spec (environmental controls)

skos:definition: The allowable ambient temperature range for paste open-life.
skos:example: Spec: 20–25 °C during use; excursions outside range end the open-life.
normative_reference: Manufacturer datasheet; internal process spec (environmental controls)

skos:definition: Maximum time an opened paste may remain in use before disposal or remix/requalification.
skos:example: Typical open-life: 8 hours on the printer at 23 °C.
normative_reference: Manufacturer datasheet; internal process spec (environmental controls)

skos:definition: Recorded duration of paste exposure on the printer for a specific run.
skos:example: Paste jar in use for 6.5 hours (within 8-hour limit).
normative_reference: Manufacturer datasheet; internal process spec (environmental controls)

skos:definition: The allowable maximum time for paste usage after opening under specified conditions.
skos:example: Spec: ≤8 hours at 20–25 °C; beyond this requires paste replacement.
normative_reference: Manufacturer datasheet; internal process spec (environmental controls)

skos:definition: Storage temperature range for sealed solder paste to maintain performance until expiry.
skos:example: Refrigerated storage at 0–10 °C per supplier datasheet.

skos:definition: Recorded storage temperature for a specific paste lot during shelf life.
skos:example: Data logger shows 5 °C ±2 °C for the entire storage period.

skos:definition: Required storage temperature range for sealed paste before opening.
skos:example: Spec: 0–10 °C; do not freeze.

skos:definition: Time interval from manufacture during which sealed paste is expected to meet specification when stored properly.
skos:example: Shelf life: 6 months from date of manufacture at 0–10 °C.

skos:definition: Recorded age of a paste lot at the time of use or inspection.
skos:example: Lot SP-22 is 4.2 months old—within 6‑month shelf life.

skos:definition: Maximum allowable time from manufacture for sealed paste, under specified storage conditions.
skos:example: Spec: ≤6 months at 0–10 °C.

skos:definition: Resistance of solder paste to flow under shear, commonly measured with a rotational viscometer (e.g., Malcom) at specified speed and temperature.
skos:example: 165 Pa·s at 25 °C and 10 rpm on a Malcom viscometer.
test_method: Malcom/Brookfield rotational viscometer at specified rpm and 25°C

skos:definition: A measured viscosity value for a specific paste lot under specified test conditions.
skos:example: Lot SP-22: 170 Pa·s (Malcom, 25 °C, 10 rpm).

skos:definition: Required viscosity range and test method for a solder paste.
skos:example: Spec: 140–220 Pa·s at 25 °C, 10 rpm (Malcom).

skos:definition: Peak reflow temperature out of the qualified window (too high or too low), resulting in poor wetting, excessive spread, or flux exhaustion.
skos:example: Measured peak 255–260 °C for SAC305 causes over‑spreading and discoloration on thin boards.
normative_reference: IPC-7530 (Temperature Profiling for Mass Soldering); JEDEC J-STD-020
normative_notes: SAC305 typical window; outside is a FailureCause

skos:definition: Increase in solder paste footprint dimensions after printing but before reflow due to low viscosity, high humidity, or long wait time.
skos:example: Within 10 minutes of print, deposits extend ~75 µm beyond pad edges on 0.5 mm pitch QFP pads.

skos:definition: Thermal process that melts solder paste and forms metallurgical joints according to a defined temperature profile (preheat, soak, reflow, cool).
skos:example: Forced‑convection reflow with SAC305: TAL 60–90 s, peak 245 °C, ramp 1 °C/s.

skos:definition: Solder paste remaining in the stencil aperture after the print stroke, reducing transfer efficiency and causing under‑deposits.
skos:example: SPI indicates 75% transfer efficiency on fine‑pitch pads; 25% residual paste visible in apertures.
normative_notes: Typical TE target ≥80% for fine pitch

skos:definition: The most fundamental, addressable cause of a problem which, if corrected, prevents recurrence.
skos:example: Investigation shows squeegee angle at 45° was the root cause of widespread bridging; corrected to 60°.

skos:definition: The metallic composition of solder (e.g., Sn–Ag–Cu) used to form joints.
skos:example: SAC305 (Sn96.5/Ag3.0/Cu0.5) for lead‑free reflow.

skos:definition: Recorded alloy designation/composition for a specific paste or solder form.
skos:example: Lot SP-22: SAC305 confirmed by CoA.

skos:definition: Required alloy family and grade for a given assembly process.
skos:example: Spec: Use SAC305 or SAC405 per customer requirement; no SnPb allowed.

skos:definition: Height of a BGA/WLCSP solder ball above the package substrate or the final stand‑off after reflow, depending on context.
skos:example: Post‑reflow stand‑off measured at 0.28 mm for a 0.30 mm ball BGA.

skos:definition: Measured solder ball height/stand‑off for a specific device or solder joint.
skos:example: X‑ray metrology: stand‑off 0.275–0.285 mm across the BGA field.

skos:definition: Required solder ball height or stand‑off range under defined reflow conditions.
skos:example: Spec: 0.27–0.31 mm post‑reflow stand‑off for 0.30 mm balls.

skos:definition: Unintended solder connection that electrically shorts adjacent conductive features after reflow.
skos:example: Bridge between pins 17–18 on a 0.5 mm pitch QFP causes ICT failure.

skos:definition: Process that transfers solder paste through a stencil onto PCB lands using a squeegee under controlled speed, pressure, and angle.
skos:example: Printing with 100 µm stainless stencil, 60° polyurethane squeegee, 40 mm/s, 5 kgf pressure.

skos:definition: Squeegee blade angle below the qualified range (e.g., <55–60°), promoting paste scooping and excess deposition.
skos:example: Angle set to 45° results in thick deposits and bridging on fine‑pitch features.
normative_notes: Typical operating range 55–65°; too low increases scooping

skos:definition: Squeegee pressure above the qualified window, causing stencil wear, understencil leakage, and smeared deposits.
skos:example: Pressure increased to 7 kgf causes paste bleed‑out under the stencil and shorts on QFN pads.
normative_notes: Absolute pressure depends on blade width; monitor for understencil leakage

skos:definition: Squeegee traverse speed below the qualified range, increasing paste dwell time and risk of over‑filling apertures.
skos:example: Reducing speed from 50 mm/s to 15 mm/s leads to over‑deposits on 0.5 mm pitch pads.
normative_notes: Typical window 30–80 mm/s; too low increases overfill

skos:definition: Flatness of the stencil underside relative to the PCB surface during printing; non‑coplanarity introduces variable gasket gaps.
skos:example: Underside gap up to 0.03 mm observed at board corner, causing thin deposits there.

skos:definition: Measured deviation from planarity between stencil underside and PCB surface.
skos:example: Feeler gauge shows 0.02–0.03 mm gap at the rear edge of the print window.

skos:definition: Allowable maximum gasket gap/flatness deviation across the print area.
skos:example: Spec: ≤0.05 mm gap anywhere within the print window.

skos:definition: Nominal thickness of the printing stencil material.
skos:example: 100 µm stainless steel stencil used for mixed‑technology build.

skos:definition: Measured stencil thickness at a specific location.
skos:example: Micrometer reading: 99.6–100.4 µm across the panel area.

skos:definition: Required stencil thickness and tolerance for the job or aperture region (including step‑downs/ups if any).
skos:example: Spec: 100 µm ±5 µm; step‑down to 80 µm in the BGA field.
normative_notes: Example spec 100 µm ±5 µm; local step-downs may apply

skos:definition: Use of a stencil thickness above the qualified value for fine‑pitch features, leading to excessive paste volume and bridging.
skos:example: 150 µm stencil used with 0.40 mm pitch BGA results in frequent shorts.

skos:definition: Temperature difference across regions of a PCB during reflow, causing uneven wetting, skew, tombstoning, or variable voiding.
skos:example: ΔT ≈ 25 °C between center and edge at peak leads to tombstoning of 0402 parts near the edge.

skos:definition: Duration that solder remains above its liquidus temperature outside the qualified window (too short or too long), affecting wetting and intermetallic growth.
skos:example: Profile shows TAL ≈ 120 s for SAC305 (too long), causing excessive spread and IMC thickening.
normative_reference: IPC-7530 (Temperature Profiling for Mass Soldering); JEDEC J-STD-020
